summary: Tested new auth features: forgot/reset password flow + admin auto-seeding + regression. Backend: 7/7 pytest cases pass (register/login/me, duplicate register, admin seed login, forgot unknown email generic response, full reset flow via log-scraped link + reused-token rejection, invalid token, admin re-seed after DB delete + supervisor restart). Frontend: all 10 UI flows pass (forgot link only in login mode, nav to /forgot-password, submit forgot form for unknown and known emails shows forgot-password-sent, /reset-password without token shows reset-missing-token, mismatched passwords -> 'Passwords don\'t match.' toast, successful reset -> redirect to /auth, reused token -> 'invalid or has expired' toast, login with new password works, admin login + /admin access confirmed showing admin tabs).

design_issues.screen: Header navbar when admin is signed in
issues: User name is literally 'Admin' which, next to the 'ADMIN' nav link, visually renders as 'ADMIN  ADMIN' side-by-side. Cosmetic only — consider renaming seeded admin to 'Site Admin' or styling the user chip differently.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py line 517: `expires_at = record and record['expires_at'].replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)` is short-circuit — fine, but the subsequent `expires_at < datetime.now(timezone.utc)` would raise TypeError if `record` is None. The `not record` check earlier prevents it due to short-circuit evaluation, so safe but fragile. Consider restructuring for clarity.
server.py seed_admin: Only logs 'Created admin account' on first create; silent on password rotation. Add logger.info when password is updated for observability.
server.py: forgot_password rate limit is purely per-IP (5/hour) — behind a proxy with shared NAT this could block legitimate users. Consider combining with per-email limit.
Reset tokens are stored hashed (sha256) which is good; however no secondary index on `user_id` for the delete_many clean-up — fine at current scale.
FRONTEND_URL is required at runtime (KeyError if missing) when forgot_password is called — add a fallback or startup assertion to fail-fast.
seed_data_creation: Each test creates a unique TEST_<uuid>@example.com user via register endpoint; no manual cleanup — these are leftover but prefixed for identification.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_auth_flows.py covers forgot/reset + admin seeding including an admin-reseed test that physically deletes the admin from Mongo and does `sudo supervisorctl restart backend`. If running repeatedly, note each run restarts the backend once. Reset link extraction reads /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log. test_api_smoke.py still exists for broader regression.
